claims.statement: Analysts can explore real database data with responsive linked views that preserve row meaning and filter scope.
Keep a complete client snapshot of authorized source tables when their rows and fields fit the workload; a full snapshot is not mandatory for every source.
The authenticated server-side customer instance owns source registration and customer identity; the browser cannot choose another instance with a client-supplied identity selector.
Incomplete data, missing fields, stale replies, and unstable identities must not claim exact exhaustive results.
Query contract, transport, adapters, and hosting are separate tracks with explicit handoffs.
The 10,000–100,000 row range and notebook encoding ideas are hypotheses, not measured budgets or fixed product limits.

themes: Named workload proof before added infrastructure

shape.appetite: One visible linked-view task and a small read contract.
shape.problem: The current workspace assumes full local rows and owner-aware Crossfilter populations. Remote partial data needs explicit identity, scope, and coverage before it can preserve those behaviors.

recommended_shape.read_boundary: Host-owned endpoint resolves registered source tables for the authenticated customer instance
recommended_shape.first_policy: Complete authorized source-table snapshots passed as fresh immutable arrays into ExplorEdaProject.tables; existing evaluator computes stages and contributors locally
recommended_shape.projection_candidate: Output-only or source-column projection is not the default or runtime fallback; consider it only when dependency closure covers every admitted operation and inspection path
recommended_shape.identity: Bind query and snapshot identities to server-owned customer instance and source registry; never trust a client-supplied customer selector
recommended_shape.coverage: State complete tables, schema, source identity, and snapshot; reject incomplete or stale replies
recommended_shape.later: Add aggregates, pages, or projection only after a named workload or required access pattern proves the need

success_moves: Resolve customer and source ownership from authenticated server-side instance state; include that identity in query and snapshot scope.
Return complete authorized source tables through ExplorEdaProject.tables so the existing evaluator preserves stages and contributors.
Represent selected, owner-excluded context, workspace, local, and facet populations explicitly.
Admit only complete snapshot replies using separate request relevance, result meaning, customer/source ownership, and source snapshot identity.
Evaluate a dependency-closed projection only as a measured candidate; do not use it as an automatic fallback.

first_proof.question: Can one complete authorized source snapshot preserve current evaluation, inspection, and linked-view behavior while stale or incomplete replies are rejected?
first_proof.artifact: Deterministic fake host reader connected to ExplorEdaProject.tables, with a hand-audited bar/scatter/Rows/stage/trace fixture and request/result trace.
first_proof.decision_rule: Keep this boundary only if stage rows, contributors, selected/context/Rows keys, and counts match the oracle and every incomplete, obsolete, mismatched, or unauthorized reply fails admission. Test projection only as a separate candidate if the complete snapshot misses an agreed workload budget.

dependencies.name: Host-owned authorized database source snapshot
dependencies.application_seam: The host authenticates the request, resolves customer identity and registered sources from server-side instance state, reads a complete bounded snapshot, then passes fresh immutable source arrays through ExplorEdaProject.tables. The existing evaluator keeps analysis, stages, contributors, and chart populations local.
failure_modes: Client-supplied customer or source identity escapes server ownership
Partial rows or fields are marked complete
Oversized snapshot exceeds the named browser budget
proof_rungs: Deterministic fake host reader with complete, error, incomplete, and reordered replies
One bounded immutable read-only PostgreSQL fixture

first_proof_role.rationale: The fake can prove host ownership, completion, immutable table handoff, evaluator stages, source contributors, and linked filtering without driver or production access.

dependencies.local_proof: Use a hand-audited source fixture and fake host reader. Verify complete arrays and customer/source scope before passing tables to ExplorEdaProject; inject delayed, failed, incomplete, wrong-schema, and wrong-instance replies and prove they cannot replace current tables.
dependencies.live_proof: After the fake passes, use one disposable read-only PostgreSQL fixture and one customer instance configuration. Verify consistent bounded source reads, scalar identity, and full completion. This does not establish support for other engines or production connectivity.
dependencies.rollout: Keep existing local/demo table input. Enable the registered-source reader only through authenticated host configuration. Reject incomplete replies; never fall back from them to partial local results. Retain the full snapshot until a dependency-closed projection passes its own proof.

fast_local_loop.notes: Existing evaluator/worker tests protect the reused local path. Add the fake-reader contract test when implementation starts; no fake-reader test exists yet.
